title: Train hopping callback waits for a getter read
evidence: Both start with current=0.2, next=0.8 and zero callbacks; setting next to 0.1 crosses the current train. At frame 1 Flutter has 1 switch callback and Incular 0. A later currentTrain read makes Incular emit it, matching again at frame 2.
impact: A consumer that depends on the switch callback but does not read the composed animation never receives it, and dependent state can stay stale. If it reads later, the callback runs late and inside the getter call.
cause: The Rust implementation samples the parents lazily instead of subscribing to their changes.
fix_direction: Observe parent value changes and perform the hop and callback when the crossing occurs, respecting callback reentrancy and disposal.
limitations: One crossing direction and the default two-train configuration are checked; disposal and reentrancy are not.

title: ReorderableDelayedDragStartListener never starts a reorder when the long-press deadline fires on a frame tick
evidence: Timeline (both twins): mount at 0 ms; frame at 16 ms; touch down at 16 ms on row 0; pump 600 ms (frame at 616 ms; the 500 ms deadline falls inside the pump); move 150 px down at 616 ms; two frames; up. Flutter: started_index 0 at 616 ms, row 0 at y 150 at 632 ms, row 1 slides up, ended_index 2 at 664 ms. Incular: started_index stays -1 for the whole run, row 0 never leaves its slot, ended_index never fires. Twin check: both use a 500 ms delay (Flutter default kLongPressTimeout; Incular LONG_PRESS_TIMEOUT through on_long_press_start), a touch pointer on both (Flutter TestGesture touch; Incular touch input), identical 16 ms frames on the fake clock, identical rows and 600 ms hold. The existing unit test crates/incular-widgets/tests/reorderable.rs delayed_listener_rejects_early_motion_and_starts_after_long_press passes; it fires the deadline on a Move event with no frame pump, and the timer-driven path does not start the drag.
impact: The delayed reorder pattern used on touch lists (long press on an item, then drag) does not reorder in a running app, where frames fire the deadline before the first move. This is the common mobile path.
cause: Hypothesis, not instrumented: the delayed listener is a long-press GestureDetector wrapping the Draggable. The Draggable immediate recognizer joins the arena with simultaneous false (interaction.rs:702). When pump_gesture_timers accepts the long press on a frame (interaction.rs:1366-1372), apply_arena_entries rejects the pending Draggable member, so the later move has no drag recognizer. The move-driven deadline in the unit test orders these differently and still passes.
fix_direction: Make the delayed listener one delayed drag recognizer (Flutter DelayedMultiDragGestureRecognizer semantics) rather than a long-press detector around an immediate drag. Add a frame-driven reorder case to the Incular unit tests.
confidence: high for the observed failure; medium for the arena mechanism
limitations: Mechanism inferred from source and the passing unit test; not isolated with a debugger. The onReorder index convention was not compared because no reorder completes.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: Form.save skips callbacks when a field is invalid

title: Negative acceleration marks gravity simulations done immediately
evidence: Both positions are 0 with an end threshold of 100 at frame 0; Flutter reports done=0, Incular reports done=1.
impact: A negative-acceleration simulation starting below its positive threshold can be treated as finished before it moves.
cause: Completion follows the acceleration direction instead of the absolute distance threshold defined by Flutter.
fix_direction: Compare position.abs() with the nonnegative end threshold for either acceleration sign.

cause: ScrollController::jump_to (controller.rs:246-266) changes the offset and dispatches only an Update notification, skipping the start/end bracket that Flutter jumpTo wraps around forcePixels.

title: Programmatic jumps omit start and end notifications
Floating headers omit Flutter's default scroll-end snap
evidence: Both controllers end at offset 60. At frame 5 Flutter's header is at [0,-60,800,10] and animates fully into view (rect [0,0,800,70] by frame 24). Incular stays at [0,-30,800,40] through the final frame. Revalidated at a19bf487.

title: CurvedAnimation can latch the wrong curve before its first running read

At frame 1 Flutter reports 0.3164 (ease-in) and Incular 0.6836 (ease-out); max difference 0.3672. crates/incular-animation/tests/flutter_animation_parity.rs:213 covers a latch with sampled values but not this unobserved sequence.

title: Singleton arena never resolves on pointer-down; first slop-crossing move is dropped under DragStartBehavior.start
evidence: sample_list_fling (six 40 px moves): Flutter offset 40 at 48 ms, Incular 0; every later offset 40 px behind; settled 1193.7479 vs 1153.7479. Same mechanism in other twins: gestures__dismissible_threshold (one 100 px move; Incular progress stays 0 and onDismissed never fires; Flutter progress 0.625 at 48 ms and dismisses at 1032 ms); gestures__draggable_drop_target (Flutter onDragStarted at 32 ms, before any move; Incular at 48 ms after the move; accepted data identical at 80 ms). See also gestures-004.
impact: Every scroll, swipe-to-dismiss and draggable drag starts one slop (18 px touch, 36 px pan) late, and the slop-crossing delta is discarded. Dismissible thresholds and scroll positions are offset by that amount.
cause: Flutter closes the arena after pointer-down and a closed arena with one member picks it (arena.dart:251-276). Incular widget arenas have no close or sole-member default (external resolver path in arena_member.rs); the recognizer accepts on the threshold-crossing move and DragStartBehavior.start drops that delta (pointer.rs:635-665). The close helper in arena_member.rs:120 is used only standalone.
fix_direction: Resolve a sole-member arena on pointer-down, as Flutter closes the arena after the press. Keep competition when several members joined. Recheck scroll, scale, dismissible and draggable starts afterwards.

title: MergeSemantics drops descendant semantics

title: Unspecified enabled state is projected as disabled

limitations: Checked through the retained tree and the AccessKit source; native assistive technology was not run.

title: Varied extent children are measured at intrinsic size

title: SliverFillRemaining without a scroll body keeps its largest past extent
evidence: Phase 0 has a 45 px adapter above a hasScrollBody:false fill; phase 1 grows the adapter to 200 px. Flutter's fill settles at 400 px (rect ending 600). Incular's fill stays at 555 px (rect ending 755) on the last two frames; size [800,555] vs [800,400], max diff 155 px.
impact: Content above a SliverFillRemaining(hasScrollBody: false) that grows leaves the fill too large, so the scroll extent is wrong and the fill overflows the viewport. Common in empty-state layouts beside a changing header.
cause: FillRemainingRenderSliver computes extent as self.extent.get().max(remaining_extent).max(child_hint); the cell keeps the largest extent from earlier layouts, so the extent never shrinks. Flutter recomputes extent from the current remaining extent on every layout.
fix_direction: Compute the non-scroll-body extent from the current remaining extent and child hint on every layout, without carrying the previous maximum forward.
limitations: Only growth of the preceding sliver was tested; shrink of the viewport and reverse axes were not. Phase change verified on a single run.

title: KeepAlive does not retain a scrolled-away child

title: Controller value listeners are change-gated
evidence: At frame 1 (16 ms) Flutter has 1 value notification and Incular 0, with value 0.25 in both. After the same-value assignment at frame 5 Flutter increments its count again and Incular does not. Max difference 3 across 21 frames.

cause: Public listener dispatch shares the state-change guard used for reactive invalidation.

limitations: Equal-value assignment and zero-elapsed tick are the only cases isolated; set_value mid-run in anim_core__controller_set_value_mid_run is not counted because its listener counts were not sampled.

title: Derived animations cannot register Flutter-style listeners

title: with_vsync tickers do not inherit TickerMode

A controller ticking through with_vsync() is scheduled outside a retained AnimationTicker node, so an ancestor TickerMode does not mute it automatically; the caller must call set_ticker_muted. The retained-tree mute check is animation_muted (interaction.rs:2187), and existing ticker_mode.rs tests cover retained-tree tickers only.

cause: Incular's self-scheduling with_vsync ticker has no widget or environment provider connection.
fix_direction: Provide a widget-aware ticker provider that updates controller mute state from the active TickerMode, or make the ownership path explicit in the public API.
limitations: Source-only. The Flutter twin would need a TickerMode toggle during a running animation; see the harness request.

title: Size and rectangle tweens clamp extrapolated extents

impact: Curves or parent animations that overshoot can produce negative size extents in Flutter, while Incular truncates them to zero. Rect tween edges then differ too.
cause: The shared Incular Size interpolation clamps negative dimensions during extrapolation.
fix_direction: Preserve signed interpolated dimensions in tween math, while keeping non-negative validation at APIs that require layout sizes.
limitations: Only progress 2 is sampled for extrapolation.

title: Tween sequences choose the previous item at an exact boundary
evidence: At progress 0.5 on a valid discontinuous boundary Flutter returns 0.7 from the second item and Incular 0.2 from the first. The flipped value is 0.3 vs 0.8 for the same boundary.
impact: A sequence whose adjacent items do not share an endpoint produces a different value exactly at the item transition.
cause: Incular's inclusive upper-bound comparison differs from Flutter's half-open interval selection.
fix_direction: Use a strict upper-bound comparison for non-final segments and keep the final segment responsible for progress 1.
limitations: Only one discontinuous boundary is sampled; continuous boundaries match.

title: Flipped tween sequences have no direct Incular equivalent
evidence: Source review. FlippedTweenSequence.transform(t) evaluates 1 - super.transform(1 - t); TweenSequence does not implement Animatable and ReverseTween does not invert the resulting value. The sequence scenario computes the formula inline on the Incular side.
impact: Callers cannot use a named flipped sequence as an animatable; they must write the reverse-and-invert expression themselves.
cause: There is no flipped sequence type, and TweenSequence is not wired into the Animatable trait used by composition.
fix_direction: Make TweenSequence usable as an Animatable and add a wrapper that evaluates 1 - sequence(1 - t).
limitations: Source-only for the missing type; the formula itself matches in the scenario.

title: Color, size, and rect tweens do not accept nullable endpoints

impact: Callers cannot fade a color to or from no color while keeping its RGB channels, or pass absent size and rect endpoints as Flutter does.
cause: Incular's typed tween aliases accept concrete Color, Size and Rect values rather than optional endpoints.
fix_direction: Add nullable tween variants or model these endpoint semantics in the corresponding typed tween APIs.
limitations: Source-only; the Rust aliases cannot express None.

title: DragTarget that rejects a candidate gets no onLeave or onMove, and nested targets do not fall through

fix_direction: Track every hit DragTarget as entered, call onMove for each, call onLeave for each on exit, and try outer targets in path order when an inner target rejects.

title: Hint and tooltip share one description field, and state.tooltip is never set

title: No semantic sort key or ordinal traversal order
evidence: Source reading at a19bf487: Flutter sorts sibling semantic nodes by SemanticsSortKey (OrdinalSortKey is the common form), so an app can reorder traversal without changing the widget tree. impact: Screen-reader order follows the widget tree. An app whose visual order differs from its reading order cannot correct it through semantics.
cause: The retained node model has no ordering key, and the semantics pass does not sort siblings.
fix_direction: Add an optional ordinal sort key to the semantic properties, and sort siblings within each parent by it (stable, with the widget order as the tiebreaker) as Flutter does.
limitations: Source-only. The ordering rule itself was not run against Flutter's sorted node output.

title: Resizing header reports pinned-header cache extent, building one trailing row too few
evidence: Collapse from 120 to 40 px with the default Pinned behaviour matches on header and body rects for frames 0-2. At offset 60 both sides place body rows at the same positions, but Flutter builds rows 20 and 21 and Incular does not. Flutter's resizing header reports cacheExtent calculateCacheOffset(from 0 to childExtent) = 60 at this offset; Incular's pinned_geometry reports -cacheOrigin + layoutExtent = 120, consuming twice the cache.
impact: Rows near the trailing cache edge after a resizing header are built later than in Flutter; no visible pixel difference at rest, but cache-dependent side effects and first-scroll readiness differ.
cause: ResizingHeaderRenderSliver uses pinned_geometry (the pinned persistent-header formula) for its cache. Flutter's pinned persistent header uses that formula, but Flutter's resizing header uses calculateCacheOffset over [0, childExtent]. Incular's pinned path matches Flutter's pinned path, so the difference is in the resizing header only.
fix_direction: Give the resizing header Flutter's calculateCacheOffset cache contribution over [0, child extent] rather than the pinned persistent-header formula.
limitations: The cause is inferred from the source formulas and the observed built set; no instrumentation of the consumed cache was added. Only the Pinned behaviour was compared, since Flutter has no scroll-behaviour enum.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: AnimatedSize retarget uses the previous animation tick

title: Children whose edge exactly meets the cache boundary are built on the opposite side
evidence: Viewport 600 px, default cache 250 px, 50 px rows. At offset 0 Flutter builds rows 0-16 and Incular 0-17; row 17 starts exactly at the cache end (850). At offset 1000 Flutter builds 14-36 and Incular 15-37; row 14 ends exactly at the cache start and row 37 starts at the cache end. Built counts are equal (17 and 23), so only the edge convention differs. A non-aligned 180 px cache on fixed 40 px rows matches.
impact: Only children that touch the cache edge exactly differ in whether they are built; nothing visible differs. Relevant only where build side effects are counted.
cause: The leading and trailing cache edges are treated as half-open in opposite directions: Flutter includes the child that ends at the cache start and excludes the child that starts at the cache end, while Incular does the reverse.
fix_direction: Align the inclusive edge rule of the materialized-row range with Flutter's child range computation.
limitations: The edge rule is inferred from the built sets; the render path that produced these sets was not traced. Only 50 px rows with 250 px cache at 600 px viewports were tested.
